## Summary
The composite claim-and-start path returns two full item snapshots with different statuses, a raw input ID, and no top-level final status or changed-field count. Plain claim follows the compact canonical receipt contract.

Reproduced with the official installed `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.9.30 on Linux, using disposable synthetic non-Git trackers. No implementation changes are included in this issue.

## Reproduction
```bash
LAB=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$LAB/home" "$LAB/work"
export HOME="$LAB/home" PM_PATH="$LAB/work/.agents/pm"
export PM_GLOBAL_PATH="$LAB/global" PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
cd "$LAB/work"
pm init "$PM_PATH" --defaults --author audit --agent-guidance skip --json >/dev/null
pm create task "Audit sample" --id t1 --description "Execution detail" --json >/dev/null
```
```bash
pm claim t1 --start --author audit --json >start.json
pm claim t1 --author audit --json >claim.json
```

## Actual
The start receipt has this shape (abridged):
```json
{
  "id": "t1",
  "action": "start_task",
  "claim": {"item": {"id":"pm-t1","status":"open"}, "changed_fields":["assignee","claim_principal"]},
  "update": {"item": {"id":"pm-t1","status":"in_progress"}, "changed_fields":["status"], "warnings":[]}
}
```
Both nested items contain the full content, not just the excerpt above. In the measured fixture, this was 1,299 bytes. Plain claim returned a 151-byte flat receipt with canonical `id: "pm-t1"`, final status and `changed_field_count`. Root help advertises the flat mutation contract.

## Expected and impact
The optimized composite command should provide a compact, unambiguous final receipt by default: canonical ID, final status, total changed-field count and concise per-stage outcomes. It should not make consumers guess whether the stale claim snapshot or the update snapshot is authoritative.

## Implementation plan
1. Route claim/start composite results through the shared mutation receipt normalization.
2. Resolve the canonical item ID once and propagate it to all top-level and stage references.
3. Derive final status from the completed operation state; avoid duplicate full item snapshots by default.
4. Preserve concise claim/update outcomes and explicit partial-failure receipts. Do not hide a successful claim if starting fails, or imply atomicity unless guaranteed.
5. Keep full stage snapshots and detailed changed fields behind an explicit documented opt-in; account for compatibility consumers and SDK/MCP parity.
6. Document composite result semantics alongside #1359's execution/checkpoint work.

## Regression acceptance
- [ ] Short and canonical input IDs produce the same canonical outer ID
- [ ] Default receipt has final status and changed-field count without duplicate item bodies
- [ ] Start success, already-owned/no-op, unavailable claim, and update-after-claim failure report truthful stage outcomes
- [ ] Full-detail opt-in is complete and consistent with the compact receipt
- [ ] JSON and default rendering share the same semantics
- [ ] Deterministic payload-size regression catches duplicate snapshot reintroduction; byte counts are not presented as provider tokens

## Ownership and duplicate check
Child of #1363; related #1359 and #1362 under #1357. Closed #437 established lean mutation defaults; this is the still-uncompacted composite path, including canonical identity and final-state ambiguity. Searched open and closed claim/start/receipt issues; #1352 is a different invalid-flag recovery failure. No implementation is included here.
